description: DWSD contains 784 photographed waste scenes with 2,350 annotated object segments across fourteen material categories. Jadavpur University and collaborating researchers collected images in West Bengal, including the university area, Garia and Berhampore, to support automated segregation of recyclable and non-recyclable waste. The article describes phone photographs and Labelme colour annotations with PNG naming. Mendeley publishes a ZIP archive free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is selected streets, parks, lawns and waste areas; calendar collection dates were not established in the reviewed metadata. The sample is an image-recognition benchmark, not a measured inventory of waste mass or collection demand. Dense overlapping objects and local scene selection are limitations for transfer to another waste stream. Modellers could test perception errors in simulations of automated sorting or waste-monitoring systems. model-dumped-waste-uav-detection offers a related detection model with different imagery. No photographs or masks were downloaded, and no segmentation model was evaluated.
